subject: Urgent: AtlasFin production retry storm, rising 5xx/429 rates — exec update & mitigation
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@atlasfin.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@atlasfin.com, devops-team@atlasfin.com
Date: 2026-03-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Unexpected surge in 5xx/429s from Redwood API - urgent

Marissa —

We started seeing elevated 5xx and 429 responses from the Redwood inference endpoint (model: rw-v2-small) starting ~08:50 PDT. Errors are spiking across multiple services, causing timeouts across our feature pipelines — our ingestion and realtime scoring are both impacted. Sample request IDs: rq_3f9a1, rq_3f9a2, rq_3f9a5 (attached a small snippet).

Traffic pattern: sudden spike at ~08:50 with a sustained elevated error rate ~15–18% for the last 20 minutes. Clients are attempting retries which seems to be amplifying the load. We are seeing increased tail latency on the SDK and several websocket disconnects.

Can you confirm receipt and give an ETA for mitigation? This is production impacting for our customers. We're happy to route a small % of traffic elsewhere or accept temporary rate limits if that helps.

Thanks,
Priya Shah
VP Engineering — AtlasFin

Attachments: support_log_snippet.txt
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@atlasfin.com>
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-03-14T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected surge in 5xx/429s from Redwood API - urgent

Priya —

Thanks for the heads-up and the logs; we've received your snippet. I’m escalating this to ops and the infra on-call now (cc’d). Immediate next steps we are starting now:

- We are throttling incoming requests from clients we detect doing aggressive retries (server-side rule) to reduce amplification.
- Flipping route to a safe model variant (rw-v2-small-fallback) for new sessions for the next 30m.
- Ops will validate autoscaler and queue backpressure signals; engineering will evaluate recent infra changes.

Quick ask: would you allow Redwood to route up to 10% of your traffic to a dedicated warm instance in our US cluster while we stabilize? That will reduce tail latency while we patch. If yes, reply "approve" and give me the earliest window (we can flip in ~12 minutes).

ETA: We expect an initial mitigation impact in 15–25 minutes; a targeted fix/patch ETA in ~90 minutes depending on root cause. We’ll send regular updates and a post-incident summary.

Apologies for the impact — we’ll keep this tightly coordinated.

—Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0182

Attachments: runbook_retry_storm.pdf
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-03-14T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: initial ops triage — AtlasFin 5xx/429s

Small ops update — observed the same spike across two US clusters (us-west-2 primary, us-east-1 fallback). Key observations:

- Queue growth began at 08:48 PDT; median service latency rose from 120ms -> 780ms; tail p99 -> ~2.3s.
- Elevated 429s correlate with a spike in short-interval retries from a subset of SDK clients (same client fingerprint as AtlasFin).
- Autoscaler reported transient underprovisioning; there was a scaling policy tweak deployed last night (dampening window increased from 30s -> 90s). This would delay scale-up during rapid bursts.

Immediate mitigations executed (completed):
- Server-side conservative reject policy applied for clients with >8 req/s sustained.
- Enabled rw-v2-small-fallback routing for new sessions for AtlasFin (10% to dedicated warm pool).
- Increased autoscaler aggressiveness back to 30s and temporarily bumped min capacity for affected pools.

Next: engineering to validate cache/kv eviction patterns and confirm whether the autoscaler tweak alone explains the tail (cc: Rishi).

—Sean
Director, Service Reliability — Redwood Inference

Command outputs (sanitized):
- flag flip: set autoscaler.dampening_window=30s -> OK
- route change: atlasfin-route=%10->dedicated-warm -> OK
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-03-14T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: initial ops triage — AtlasFin 5xx/429s

Quick root-cause traction from infra:

- Confirmed the autoscaler damping change is the primary amplifier. When traffic rose quickly the scheduler delayed pod spin-up; queues increased and triggered per-worker memory pressure.
- There is a secondary symptom: a cache-eviction regression introduced in a commit last week (eviction loop under specific seq-len distribution) which caused a CPU spike for certain requests; that contributed to worker slowdown.

Planned fixes:
1) Roll back damping window (done) and monitor; we already saw a reduction in queue growth after the flip.
2) Push hotfix to skip the pathological eviction path (patch attached as rollback_patch.diff). Testing on canary nodes now.
3) If metrics still degrade, we'll route AtlasFin traffic fully to a pre-warmed dedicated instance (we have capacity in us-west-2); need customer approval to change routing.

Estimated times: canary test results in 20–30 minutes; hotfix rollout another 30–45 minutes after validation.

We should coordinate a status page entry once we have canary metrics.

—Rishi
Staff Software Engineer — Redwood Inference

Attachments: rollback_patch.diff
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@atlasfin.com>, Anand Rao <anand.rao@atlasfin.com>
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-03-14T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Status update: mitigation in place — next ETA and ask for routing permission

Priya / Anand —

Status update and apology for the impact. Summary of what we've done so far:
- Applied conservative server-side retry throttles for aggressive clients.
- Temporarily routed 10% of your new sessions to a pre-warmed dedicated pool to reduce tail latency.
- Reverted autoscaler dampening window to 30s; queue growth has started to recede in the past 10 minutes.
- Engineering running a canary with the eviction hotfix; initial canary metrics look promising (p50/p95 improved).

Next ETA: we expect to complete a safe rollout of the eviction hotfix across affected pools in ~75 minutes, barring regressions. Full normalization (error rates <1%) targeted within 90–120 minutes.

Permission request: routing AtlasFin traffic fully to a dedicated instance would eliminate cross-tenant interference but will change your billing for that window (we can credit for impact; see compensation note below). Please reply with "approve routing" if you consent and we will initiate the full cutover (estimated flip time ~10 minutes).

Status page and external comms: we have a draft status update (link below). Would you like us to post an update referencing AtlasFin by name, or keep the message generic? We can coordinate a joint statement if helpful.

We will continue to send 30-minute updates until we are normalized. Escalating to our executive team internally; Karthik is standing by for any contract/SLA questions.

Again, we are sorry for the disruption — you have my attention until this is resolved.

—Marissa
Senior Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference

Related link: https://drive.redwood.ai/d/1a2b3c-draft-status-update

Thanks for the quick response and the clear steps. We approve routing — please proceed with full cutover to the dedicated instance. We expect this to be used for the next 3 hours while you stabilize.

We also want the status page public update to be generic (no customer name) — please coordinate timing with our ops lead (copied).

Also, per our SLA, we'd like to discuss credits for the window of impact; Anand and I will expect a post-incident credit proposal.

Appreciate the rapid coordination — please keep us posted.

—Priya
VP Engineering — AtlasFin
